The court should apply Washington law and deny the punitive damages claim, because a federal court in Washington applies Washington's choice-of-law rules and Washington bars punitive damages absent statute. Neither option in the note fits well: federal common law does not govern a state-law tort claim under *Erie*, and California's rule would control only if Washington's choice-of-law analysis points to California and overrides its own public policy, which I have not verified. I have not checked current Washington authority on how its courts treat punitive damages in conflicts cases.

CONFIDENCE: 45
